name: Optimal Fixed-Rank Parent after Deleting a Minimum Section
statement: Let $M$ be maximum of rank $r$, let $J$ have size $q$ with $1\le q\le r$, and suppose the section $S=M[p]$ is contained in every other $J$-section, equivalently $S=\partial_JM$. Deleting all words of $M$ with $J$-pattern $p$ yields a class with a rank-$r$ maximum parent using exactly $r+1-q$ auxiliaries, and no rank-$r$ parent retaining the original visible coordinates uses fewer.
proof: Choose a decreasing maximum sequence inside the minimum section. At each step construct a rank-$(r-1)$ maximum subclass of the current parent whose marked $J$-section is the next sequence level, then exchange the removed layer between two heights of one new auxiliary. The union and intersection of the shores have ranks $r$ and $r-1$, and a missing-trace argument gives the VC bound. After $r-q+1$ steps the marked section is empty. Conversely the absent pattern consisting of $p$ and the auxiliary mark needs at least $r+1$ coordinates in a rank-$r$ maximum class, so at least $r+1-q$ auxiliaries are necessary.
